text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The water level of the Kunene River is continuing to drop and by the end of this week could fall to an all-time low of 24 or 25 cubic metres an hour, badly affecting the electricity generating capacity of the Ruacana hydro-electric power station.
- Former plan fighters protesting for jobs are sceptical about the job offers extended to them by a special cabinet committee set up to deal with their unemployment problems.
- Windhoek's townplanners have about 5,000 hectares left for extension of the capital, which currently covers 8,000 hectares of built-up land.
- Former plan fighters protesting for jobs are adamant they will remain at the Windhoek showgrounds until the president grants them an audience.

- The services of about 50 percent of the workforce of the SWAPO-controlled company Kuiseb Fishing and the fishing company of Ohlthaver and List have been terminated scarcely two weeks after the announcement of the merger between Kuiseb Fishing, Foodcon and Irvin & Johnson.
- The Namibian Breweries Ltd (NBL) yesterday denied that it has broken Southern African Customs Union agreements and has not paid the full taxes on its beer marketed in the region.
